t: A county on the North Sea coast, founded in 862, whose counts held most of it from France and a smaller part from the German emperors.
Its cloth towns of Ghent, Bruges and Ypres made it one of the wealthiest and most urbanised regions of medieval Europe.
It passed to Burgundy in 1384, then to the Habsburgs, lost its south to France, and was annexed by France in 1795.
dyk: Flanders’ founder, Baldwin Iron Arm, won his county by eloping with Judith, a Carolingian princess who had already been married to two kings of Wessex, father and son.
ev: Baldwin Iron Arm elopes with Judith, daughter of Charles the Bald
Count Charles the Good is murdered in Bruges
Baldwin IX becomes the first Latin emperor of Constantinople
Flemish militias defeat French knights at the Battle of the Golden Spurs
Edward III is proclaimed king of France at Ghent
Flanders passes to Philip the Bold of Burgundy

f.successor: Burgundian State (from 1384); annexed by France in 1795
